entities.summary: Pabag, an Iranian prince, ruled Stakhr, the capital of Pars, from 205 or 206 until his death sometime between 207 and 210. He was succeeded by his eldest son, Shapur. Pabag's reign was marked by the establishment of the Sasanian Empire's core institutions and the consolidation of Parsian power. The empire's military campaigns and administrative reforms were largely driven by Pabag's successors, including Ardashir I, who would go on to establish the Sasanian Empire as a major power in the ancient Near East. Pabag's legacy is reflected in the enduring cultural and historical significance of the Sasanian Empire, which played a pivotal role in the development of Persian culture and the spread of Zoroastrianism throughout the ancient world.
